title: Exam Simulation 05
kind: Original practice exam. Not an official ISACA exam or score predictor.

questions.question: The chief audit executive is asked by the CFO to delay issuing a report on weak payment controls until after the year-end close. What should the chief audit executive do FIRST?
choices: Agree to the delay because year-end close is a critical business period and the findings can wait
Issue the report only to the CFO to avoid wider disruption
Remove the payment findings and audit them again next year
Inform the audit committee of the request and the planned reporting timeline
questions.explanation: The audit committee oversees audit independence; pressure to delay reporting must be escalated to it.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Accepting management pressure impairs independence.
Not the best answer. Restricting distribution to the requester undermines reporting to governance.
Not the best answer. Suppressing findings breaches professional standards.
Best answer. The audit committee oversees audit independence; pressure to delay reporting must be escalated to it.

questions.question: An IS auditor was the project lead for a new access management system before joining internal audit six months ago. The audit plan now includes a review of that system. What is the BEST course of action?
choices: Perform the review because six months have passed since the move
Limit the review to areas the auditor did not personally design
Disclose the impairment and have another auditor perform the review
Perform the review but ask the system owner to sign off the work papers
questions.explanation: Auditing one’s own recent work is a self-review threat; disclosure and reassignment preserve objectivity.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Elapsed time alone does not remove a self-review threat.
Not the best answer. The auditor’s involvement still taints the overall conclusion.
Best answer. Auditing one’s own recent work is a self-review threat; disclosure and reassignment preserve objectivity.
Not the best answer. Auditee sign-off does not restore auditor independence.

questions.question: Which document should grant the internal audit function unrestricted access to records, personnel and systems?
choices: Information security policy issued by the CISO
Annual audit plan approved by the CIO
Audit charter approved by the audit committee
Engagement letter for each individual audit
questions.explanation: The audit charter establishes authority and access for the audit function as a whole.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. The security policy does not establish the audit mandate.
Not the best answer. The CIO is an auditee and cannot grant audit authority.
Best answer. The audit charter establishes authority and access for the audit function as a whole.
Not the best answer. Engagement letters cover single engagements, not overall authority.

questions.question: A company relies on a payroll provider’s SOC 1 Type 1 report covering controls as at 30 June. The audit period is the full calendar year. What is the GREATEST limitation of this report?
choices: It does not show that controls operated effectively during the year
It does not cover the provider’s information security policy, incident handling or physical security controls
It was issued by an independent service auditor
It only describes controls relevant to financial reporting
questions.explanation: A Type 1 report covers design at a point in time; operating effectiveness over the period is untested.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. A Type 1 report covers design at a point in time; operating effectiveness over the period is untested.
Not the best answer. Policy coverage is secondary to evidence of operation.
Not the best answer. Independence of the service auditor is a strength.
Not the best answer. Financial reporting focus is appropriate for payroll.

questions.question: Which type of engagement BEST evaluates the controls over an entire order-to-cash process, including the application, the infrastructure it runs on and the financial results it produces?
choices: Integrated audit
Compliance audit
Forensic audit
Administrative audit
questions.explanation: An integrated audit combines financial, operational and IS audit procedures across a process.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. An integrated audit combines financial, operational and IS audit procedures across a process.
Not the best answer. A compliance audit checks adherence to specific requirements only.
Not the best answer. A forensic audit investigates suspected fraud or crime.
Not the best answer. An administrative audit focuses on operational efficiency.

questions.question: During an investigation of suspected data theft, an IS auditor collects a laptop for analysis. What is MOST important to ensure the evidence can be used in legal proceedings?
choices: Maintaining a documented chain of custody
Analysing the original disk to save time
Copying relevant files to a shared audit folder
Asking the suspect to confirm the files found
questions.explanation: Chain of custody proves the evidence has not been altered and is admissible.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Chain of custody proves the evidence has not been altered and is admissible.
Not the best answer. Working on the original risks altering evidence.
Not the best answer. Copying files to shared folders breaks integrity and custody.
Not the best answer. A suspect’s confirmation is not a substitute for preserved evidence.

questions.question: An IS auditor has limited time to plan next year’s audits across 40 applications. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
choices: Ask each business unit which applications they would most like audited and schedule those first in the plan
Audit each application once every 40 months on a rotation
Audit applications that had findings last year only
Rank applications by business criticality and risk and audit the highest first
questions.explanation: Risk-based planning directs limited resources to the areas of greatest exposure.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Auditee preference is not a risk-based criterion.
Not the best answer. Fixed rotation ignores differences in risk.
Not the best answer. Prior findings are one input, not the full risk picture.
Best answer. Risk-based planning directs limited resources to the areas of greatest exposure.

questions.question: Which risk can the IS auditor directly control when planning an audit?
choices: Inherent risk
Control risk
Business risk
Detection risk
questions.explanation: The nature, timing and extent of audit procedures determine detection risk.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Inherent risk exists before controls and is not influenced by the auditor.
Not the best answer. Control risk depends on management’s controls.
Not the best answer. Business risk is owned by management.
Best answer. The nature, timing and extent of audit procedures determine detection risk.

questions.question: A new privacy regulation takes effect halfway through the audit year. What should the IS auditor do FIRST?
choices: Add a full privacy audit to next year’s plan
Wait for the regulator’s first enforcement action
Reassess the audit plan for areas affected by the regulation
Ask legal to confirm whether audit should be involved
questions.explanation: Significant changes in the risk environment require the risk assessment and plan to be revisited.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Deferring to next year may leave a significant risk unaddressed.
Not the best answer. Waiting for enforcement is reactive.
Best answer. Significant changes in the risk environment require the risk assessment and plan to be revisited.
Not the best answer. Legal input is useful but the audit plan is audit’s responsibility.

questions.question: A small branch cannot separate the duties of creating and approving vendor payments. Which control BEST reduces the risk?
choices: A stronger password policy for the branch payment system with monthly changes and complexity rules
Annual security awareness training for branch staff
Independent daily review of payment logs by a manager at head office
Encrypting the vendor master file
questions.explanation: When segregation is not possible, a compensating detective review by an independent person reduces the risk.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Passwords do not address the conflict of duties.
Not the best answer. Training does not prevent misuse by the person holding both duties.
Best answer. When segregation is not possible, a compensating detective review by an independent person reduces the risk.
Not the best answer. Encryption protects confidentiality, not payment authorization.

questions.question: Which control type is a reconciliation of daily batch totals between two systems?
choices: Preventive
Deterrent
Detective
Directive
questions.explanation: Reconciliation identifies discrepancies after processing has occurred.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Preventive controls stop errors before they occur.
Not the best answer. Deterrent controls discourage behaviour.
Best answer. Reconciliation identifies discrepancies after processing has occurred.
Not the best answer. Directive controls instruct or require behaviour.

questions.question: An IS auditor finds that IT general controls over change management are ineffective. What is the MOST significant impact on the audit?
choices: Only manual controls need to be reported
Reliance cannot be placed on automated application controls without further testing
The change management finding should be excluded from the report because it is outside the agreed audit scope
The audit must be terminated and reported as incomplete
questions.explanation: Weak ITGCs mean automated controls may have been altered, so they cannot be relied on without more testing.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Automated controls are also affected and must be considered.
Best answer. Weak ITGCs mean automated controls may have been altered, so they cannot be relied on without more testing.
Not the best answer. The finding is directly relevant to reliance and must be reported.
Not the best answer. Termination is not required; scope and procedures are adjusted.

questions.question: During fieldwork, the auditee asks the IS auditor to also review a new cloud application that was not in the agreed scope. What should the auditor do?
choices: Review the application informally without documentation
Assess the request, agree any scope change with the audit manager and document it
Add the application to the fieldwork immediately so the auditee stays satisfied and cooperative throughout
Refuse because scope changes are never permitted
questions.explanation: Scope changes are possible but must be evaluated, approved and documented.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Undocumented work cannot support conclusions.
Best answer. Scope changes are possible but must be evaluated, approved and documented.
Not the best answer. Unplanned additions can compromise resources and quality.
Not the best answer. Scope can change if properly controlled.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of reviewing audit work papers before the report is issued?
choices: To allow the auditee to correct the auditors’ notes
To measure how long each auditor spent on tasks
To check the spelling and formatting of findings
To confirm that evidence supports the conclusions reached
questions.explanation: Supervisory review ensures findings are supported by sufficient, appropriate evidence.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Auditees do not edit audit work papers.
Not the best answer. Time tracking is a management matter, not the purpose of review.
Not the best answer. Formatting is minor compared with evidential support.
Best answer. Supervisory review ensures findings are supported by sufficient, appropriate evidence.

questions.question: Which is the MOST appropriate response when an IS auditor discovers indicators of fraud during a routine audit?
choices: Ignore the indicators because fraud detection is not part of the agreed audit objectives or the engagement letter
Report the indicators to the appropriate level of management or the audit committee
Interview the suspected employee to obtain a confession
Expand testing until fraud is proven beyond doubt
questions.explanation: Auditors communicate fraud indicators to the right authority; investigation follows established procedures.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Ignoring indicators breaches due professional care.
Best answer. Auditors communicate fraud indicators to the right authority; investigation follows established procedures.
Not the best answer. Confronting suspects may compromise an investigation.
Not the best answer. Auditors are not required to prove fraud before reporting.

questions.question: An IS auditor wants to estimate the rate of access requests approved without a manager’s signature. Which sampling method is MOST appropriate?
choices: Discovery sampling
Attribute sampling
Haphazard sampling
Variable sampling
questions.explanation: Attribute sampling estimates how often a characteristic (a control exception) occurs.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Discovery sampling only detects whether at least one exception exists.
Best answer. Attribute sampling estimates how often a characteristic (a control exception) occurs.
Not the best answer. Haphazard selection is not statistical and gives no rate estimate.
Not the best answer. Variable sampling estimates monetary amounts.

questions.question: Compliance testing shows that a key reconciliation control is not operating. What should the IS auditor do NEXT?
choices: Retest the control with a larger sample until it passes
Rely on management’s statement that the control usually works
Increase substantive testing of the related balances
Stop testing and report that no assurance can be given
questions.explanation: When controls fail, more substantive testing is needed to reach a conclusion on the data.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Retesting until a pass is achieved is biased.
Not the best answer. Management statements are weak evidence.
Best answer. When controls fail, more substantive testing is needed to reach a conclusion on the data.
Not the best answer. The auditor can still obtain assurance through substantive work.

questions.question: Which change would require a LARGER statistical sample?
choices: Reducing the expected error rate
Increasing the confidence level
Reducing the population variability
Increasing the tolerable error rate
questions.explanation: Higher confidence requires more items to be tested.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. A lower expected error rate allows a smaller sample.
Best answer. Higher confidence requires more items to be tested.
Not the best answer. Less variability allows a smaller sample.
Not the best answer. A higher tolerable error allows a smaller sample.

questions.question: Which evidence is MOST reliable for confirming that terminated employees lost system access?
choices: A signed memo from the IT manager confirming that all leavers in the period were removed from every system
Comparison of the HR termination list with system account status extracted by the auditor
A screenshot provided by the system administrator
Interviews with team managers about recent leavers
questions.explanation: Data obtained directly by the auditor and compared to an independent source is the most reliable.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. A memo is management’s assertion.
Best answer. Data obtained directly by the auditor and compared to an independent source is the most reliable.
Not the best answer. Auditee-provided screenshots can be selective or altered.
Not the best answer. Interviews are verbal, unverified evidence.

questions.question: An IS auditor observes a backup operator performing a restore test. What is the MAIN limitation of this evidence?
choices: It is less reliable than an interview with the operator
It shows only that the procedure worked at the time observed
It cannot be documented in the work papers
It violates the operator’s confidentiality
questions.explanation: Observation provides evidence only for the moment it was made.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Observation is generally stronger than interview.
Best answer. Observation provides evidence only for the moment it was made.
Not the best answer. Observations can and should be documented.
Not the best answer. Observing work duties does not breach confidentiality.

questions.question: An IS auditor receives a vendor’s security questionnaire answered by the vendor. How should the auditor treat this evidence?
choices: As sufficient evidence because it is in writing
As a starting point that requires corroboration
As irrelevant because it comes from a third party
As stronger evidence than an independent assurance report
questions.explanation: Self-assessments are useful but need corroboration with independent evidence.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Written form does not make it independent.
Best answer. Self-assessments are useful but need corroboration with independent evidence.
Not the best answer. It is relevant, just not sufficient alone.
Not the best answer. Independent reports are more reliable than self-assessment.

questions.question: Which technique would BEST identify duplicate vendor payments across three years of transactions?
choices: Reviewing the payment procedure document
Selecting a judgmental sample of the largest payments made to each vendor in the three-year period
Running data analytics on the full payment population
Interviewing accounts payable staff
questions.explanation: Analytics over the whole population can find all duplicates efficiently.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Procedures describe intent, not actual payments.
Not the best answer. A sample may miss duplicates.
Best answer. Analytics over the whole population can find all duplicates efficiently.
Not the best answer. Interviews do not reveal transaction-level duplicates.

questions.question: An integrated test facility is used in a live payroll system. What is the GREATEST risk?
choices: Test transactions affecting real payroll totals if not reversed
Audit staff needing standing access to the production payroll system throughout the year
The test entity being visible to payroll clerks
Increased processing time for the payroll run
questions.explanation: ITF data must be isolated or reversed so it does not corrupt production results.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. ITF data must be isolated or reversed so it does not corrupt production results.
Not the best answer. Access can be controlled; the main risk is data contamination.
Not the best answer. Visibility is a minor concern compared with corrupted results.
Not the best answer. Performance impact is usually small.

questions.question: Before analysing data extracted from a production system, what should the IS auditor do FIRST?
choices: Select the analytics tool with the most features
Delete fields that appear irrelevant
Verify the completeness and accuracy of the extracted data
Present preliminary results to management
questions.explanation: Analysis of incomplete or inaccurate data leads to wrong conclusions.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Tool selection is secondary to data integrity.
Not the best answer. Removing data before validation may lose evidence.
Best answer. Analysis of incomplete or inaccurate data leads to wrong conclusions.
Not the best answer. Results should not be shared before data is validated.

questions.question: Management disagrees with an audit finding about excessive privileged access. How should the IS auditor proceed?
choices: Report the finding with management’s response and the auditor’s position
Downgrade the finding to an observation
Remove the finding from the report to maintain a good working relationship with management for future audits
Delay the report until management agrees
questions.explanation: The report should present the finding and management’s view; disagreement does not remove a valid finding.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. The report should present the finding and management’s view; disagreement does not remove a valid finding.
Not the best answer. Changing the rating without new evidence lacks objectivity.
Not the best answer. Removing valid findings breaches standards.
Not the best answer. Indefinite delay prevents timely reporting.

questions.question: Six months after the audit, management states all corrective actions are complete. What should the IS auditor do?
choices: Ask the external auditor to confirm closure
Wait until the next full audit to check
Close the findings based on management’s written statement that all agreed corrective actions are complete
Perform follow-up procedures to verify the actions are implemented and effective
questions.explanation: Follow-up must verify implementation, not rely on management assertions.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Internal audit is responsible for its own follow-up.
Not the best answer. Waiting may leave risks unaddressed.
Not the best answer. Assertions are not evidence of closure.
Best answer. Follow-up must verify implementation, not rely on management assertions.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY benefit of a control self-assessment program?
choices: It removes the need for documented evidence
It replaces the need for an internal audit function
Business staff take ownership of identifying and monitoring controls
It allows auditors to design and implement controls for the business so that weaknesses are fixed faster
questions.explanation: CSA builds control ownership and awareness within the business.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Evidence is still needed for assurance.
Not the best answer. CSA complements, not replaces, internal audit.
Best answer. CSA builds control ownership and awareness within the business.
Not the best answer. Auditors facilitate; they do not design business controls.

questions.question: A company plans to launch a service in a new country. Which action should the IS auditor expect management to take FIRST regarding compliance?
choices: Identify the legal and regulatory requirements that apply in that country
Purchase cyber insurance for the new operations
Request an external audit after launch
Implement exactly the same controls that are used in the home country so the group remains consistent everywhere
questions.explanation: Obligations must be identified before controls can be designed to meet them.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Obligations must be identified before controls can be designed to meet them.
Not the best answer. Insurance does not ensure compliance.
Not the best answer. Post-launch audit is too late to design compliance.
Not the best answer. Home-country controls may not meet local laws.

questions.question: Which is the BEST indicator that IT strategy is aligned with business strategy?
choices: IT has the largest share of the corporate budget
IT initiatives are prioritised against documented business objectives by business and IT leaders
IT staff hold up-to-date technical certifications and attend industry conferences on emerging technologies
The CIO reports directly to the CFO
questions.explanation: Alignment is shown when business objectives drive IT priorities through joint governance.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Budget size does not show alignment.
Best answer. Alignment is shown when business objectives drive IT priorities through joint governance.
Not the best answer. Certifications show skills, not alignment.
Not the best answer. Reporting line alone does not ensure alignment.

questions.question: Which body is MOST appropriate to approve and prioritise a portfolio of IT projects?
choices: IT strategy committee of the board
Information security team
IT steering committee
Project management office
questions.explanation: The steering committee, with business and IT executives, prioritises and approves projects and investments.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. The board strategy committee sets direction, not project priorities.
Not the best answer. Security advises on risk but does not prioritise the portfolio.
Best answer. The steering committee, with business and IT executives, prioritises and approves projects and investments.
Not the best answer. The PMO supports delivery but does not set business priorities.

questions.question: An IS auditor finds that developers can move their own code into production. What is the PRIMARY risk?
choices: Unauthorized or untested changes reaching production
Reduced developer productivity
Slower release cycles for urgent fixes
Higher licensing costs for development tools that are also installed in the production environment
questions.explanation: This breaks segregation of duties and allows unapproved changes.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. This breaks segregation of duties and allows unapproved changes.
Not the best answer. Productivity is not the primary control risk.
Not the best answer. The concern is control, not speed.
Not the best answer. Licensing is unrelated.

questions.question: Which governance activity belongs to the board rather than management in COBIT 2019?
choices: Planning and building IT solutions
Evaluating, directing and monitoring enterprise I&T
Monitoring service desk performance
Running day-to-day IT operations
questions.explanation: Governance evaluates, directs and monitors; management plans, builds, runs and monitors.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Building solutions is management’s role.
Best answer. Governance evaluates, directs and monitors; management plans, builds, runs and monitors.
Not the best answer. Service desk monitoring is operational management.
Not the best answer. Operations are management’s role.

questions.question: An IS auditor finds that the information security policy was last approved four years ago. What is the GREATEST concern?
choices: The policy may be too long to read
The policy may not have a version number, an owner’s name or a footer showing its classification
Staff may not know the policy exists
The policy may not reflect current risks, technology and regulations
questions.explanation: Outdated policies may not address the current threat and regulatory environment.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Length is a usability issue.
Not the best answer. Version numbering is administrative.
Not the best answer. Awareness is important but secondary to relevance.
Best answer. Outdated policies may not address the current threat and regulatory environment.

questions.question: Which is a characteristic of a standard rather than a guideline?
choices: It is mandatory and supports a policy
It gives detailed steps to perform a task
It describes recommended good practice
It states management’s overall intent
questions.explanation: Standards are mandatory requirements supporting policy.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Standards are mandatory requirements supporting policy.
Not the best answer. Procedures give step-by-step instructions.
Not the best answer. Guidelines are recommended practice.
Not the best answer. Policies state management intent.

questions.question: A business unit wants an exception to the password standard for a legacy system. What should be in place?
choices: A documented risk assessment, compensating controls and approval by the risk owner
Verbal approval from the IT manager
An instruction to staff not to discuss the exception outside the business unit until the system is replaced
Removal of the system from the asset inventory
questions.explanation: Exceptions must be risk-assessed, approved and tracked.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Exceptions must be risk-assessed, approved and tracked.
Not the best answer. Verbal approval is not auditable.
Not the best answer. Secrecy does not manage risk.
Not the best answer. Hiding the asset removes oversight.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY benefit of enterprise architecture to IT governance?
choices: It guides investment decisions toward a consistent target state
It replaces the need for project management
It documents only the network topology
It ensures that all applications across the enterprise are purchased from the same strategic technology vendor
questions.explanation: EA links business strategy to technology decisions and reduces duplication.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. EA links business strategy to technology decisions and reduces duplication.
Not the best answer. EA does not replace project management.
Not the best answer. EA covers business, data, application and technology layers.
Not the best answer. Single-vendor policies are not the goal of EA.

questions.question: A new project proposes a database platform not in the approved technology standards. What should the IS auditor expect?
choices: Installation in production to test compatibility
An architecture review and formal approval of the exception
Approval of the platform as long as the project budget can absorb any extra licensing and support costs
Immediate rejection of the project
questions.explanation: Deviations from the target architecture should be reviewed and approved.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Production experiments create unmanaged risk.
Best answer. Deviations from the target architecture should be reviewed and approved.
Not the best answer. Budget alone does not address architecture risk.
Not the best answer. Exceptions can be justified.

questions.question: Who should accept residual risk for a business application?
choices: The external auditor at year end
The business risk owner within the defined risk appetite
The IT administrator who runs the system day to day and best understands its technical weaknesses
The IS auditor after testing controls
questions.explanation: Risk acceptance is a management decision by the accountable owner.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. External auditors do not own the organisation’s risks.
Best answer. Risk acceptance is a management decision by the accountable owner.
Not the best answer. Administrators lack authority over business risk.
Not the best answer. Auditors must not accept risk.

questions.question: Which is the FIRST step in a risk assessment?
choices: Identify and value the information assets
Purchase risk management software
Select controls from a framework
Calculate the annual loss expectancy
questions.explanation: Assets must be identified before threats, vulnerabilities and impacts can be assessed.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Assets must be identified before threats, vulnerabilities and impacts can be assessed.
Not the best answer. Tools are not the first step.
Not the best answer. Controls come after risks are understood.
Not the best answer. ALE needs asset values and threat rates first.

questions.question: A risk register shows many high risks with no owner assigned. What is the MAIN concern?
choices: The register format is inconsistent
The register is too large to review
The risk ratings may be too conservative and overstate the exposure reported to the board
Risks may not be treated because no one is accountable
questions.explanation: Without ownership, risk treatment and monitoring are unlikely to happen.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Format is secondary.
Not the best answer. Size is not the main issue.
Not the best answer. Conservative ratings are less important than accountability.
Best answer. Without ownership, risk treatment and monitoring are unlikely to happen.

questions.question: A company plans to use customer purchase history for a new marketing analytics project. What should be performed FIRST?
choices: A review of the marketing budget
A penetration test of the analytics platform
A user acceptance test of the dashboards
A privacy impact assessment
questions.explanation: A PIA identifies privacy risks and lawful basis before personal data is used in new ways.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Budget is unrelated to privacy risk.
Not the best answer. Security testing comes later and does not address lawful use.
Not the best answer. UAT checks functionality, not privacy.
Best answer. A PIA identifies privacy risks and lawful basis before personal data is used in new ways.

questions.question: What is the MAIN difference between privacy and confidentiality?
choices: Confidentiality applies only to paper records
Privacy concerns individuals’ rights over their personal data; confidentiality protects any information from disclosure
There is no difference between the two terms
Privacy applies only to health data
questions.explanation: Privacy is about rights and appropriate use of personal data; confidentiality is about protecting information.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Confidentiality covers all formats.
Best answer. Privacy is about rights and appropriate use of personal data; confidentiality is about protecting information.
Not the best answer. The terms have distinct meanings.
Not the best answer. Privacy covers all personal data.

questions.question: Who is responsible for classifying a customer database?
choices: The information security officer
The database administrator
The data owner in the business
The IS auditor
questions.explanation: Data owners understand the value and sensitivity of data and decide classification.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Security advises but does not own the data.
Not the best answer. DBAs are custodians implementing controls.
Best answer. Data owners understand the value and sensitivity of data and decide classification.
Not the best answer. Auditors evaluate, not classify.

questions.question: Which is the BEST evidence that data classification is effective?
choices: A training slide explaining the classification levels that is shown to all employees during induction
Handling controls such as encryption and access restrictions match each classification level
An inventory listing all databases
A classification policy approved by the board
questions.explanation: Effectiveness is shown when controls applied match the assigned classification.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Training shows awareness only.
Best answer. Effectiveness is shown when controls applied match the assigned classification.
Not the best answer. An inventory without classification controls is incomplete.
Not the best answer. A policy shows intent, not operation.

questions.question: Which HR control BEST helps detect fraud by employees in sensitive roles?
choices: Annual performance appraisals
Background checks at hiring
Signed acceptable-use agreements
Mandatory leave with duties performed by someone else
questions.explanation: When someone else performs the duties, concealed fraud is more likely to surface.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Appraisals assess performance, not fraud.
Not the best answer. Background checks are preventive at hiring only.
Not the best answer. Agreements set expectations but do not detect fraud.
Best answer. When someone else performs the duties, concealed fraud is more likely to surface.

questions.question: An organisation has one administrator who knows how to run its core banking batch processes. What is the PRIMARY risk?
choices: Key-person dependency affecting continuity of operations
Higher salary costs for the administrator
Lack of segregation between the developers and the testers who work on the core banking batch processes
Excessive documentation of procedures
questions.explanation: Reliance on one person threatens operations if that person is unavailable.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Reliance on one person threatens operations if that person is unavailable.
Not the best answer. Cost is secondary.
Not the best answer. Developer/tester segregation is a different issue.
Not the best answer. Excess documentation is not the problem.

questions.question: Which contract clause is MOST important to allow the organisation to verify a cloud provider’s controls?
choices: A requirement that the provider’s main data centre is located in the capital city near the head office
Right to audit or to receive independent assurance reports
Free training for the customer’s staff
Fixed pricing for three years
questions.explanation: Assurance rights let the customer verify controls it remains accountable for.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Location matters for law, not verification.
Best answer. Assurance rights let the customer verify controls it remains accountable for.
Not the best answer. Training does not verify controls.
Not the best answer. Pricing does not provide assurance.

questions.question: A critical vendor has repeatedly missed SLA targets. What should the IS auditor recommend FIRST?
choices: Use the contract’s performance management and escalation provisions
Bring the service in-house without analysis
Terminate the contract immediately
Ignore the missed targets as long as users have not raised formal complaints with the service desk
questions.explanation: Contractual mechanisms should be applied before drastic action.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Contractual mechanisms should be applied before drastic action.
Not the best answer. Insourcing without analysis may increase risk.
Not the best answer. Immediate termination may disrupt operations.
Not the best answer. Missed SLAs are a risk even without complaints.

questions.question: After outsourcing the help desk, who remains accountable for protecting customer data handled by the provider?
choices: The regulator
The provider’s subcontractors
The service provider only
The outsourcing organisation
questions.explanation: Accountability cannot be transferred, even when the activity is outsourced.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Regulators supervise but are not accountable.
Not the best answer. Subcontractors are further removed.
Not the best answer. The provider is responsible for performance under contract, but accountability stays with the customer.

questions.question: Which metric is a key risk indicator rather than a key performance indicator?

questions.question: IT reports 99.9% availability, but users report frequent outages. What should the IS auditor do FIRST?

Survey users to replace the IT metric

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of an IT balanced scorecard?

To measure IT performance against business-related goals
To replace financial reporting

questions.question: Which is MOST important for an effective IT quality assurance function?

Performing all testing on behalf of users
Using only automated tools
Independence from the teams whose work it reviews

questions.question: A project is 40% complete but has used 70% of its budget. Which technique would BEST give management an objective view of progress?

Gantt chart review
Critical path method
Earned value analysis

questions.question: Users keep adding new features during development without formal approval. What is the GREATEST risk?

Scope creep causing cost and schedule overruns
Simplified testing, because users who requested the features are already closely involved in development
Reduced need for documentation

questions.question: Who should be accountable for the business case and benefits of a new CRM project?

questions.question: During a mid-project review, the expected savings in the business case are no longer achievable. What should happen NEXT?

Continue the project without change because the funds were already approved by the steering committee at the start
Hide the change until implementation
Present an updated business case to the decision body to continue, change or stop the project

questions.question: In an agile project, which control is MOST important for an IS auditor to verify?

Security and control requirements are included in the backlog and acceptance criteria
Each sprint lasts exactly two weeks
The product owner writes the code reviews

questions.question: A company buys a critical application from a small vendor. Which clause BEST protects it if the vendor goes out of business?

Vendor-provided training
Source code escrow
Annual licence renewal

questions.question: What is the MAIN risk of prototyping without controls?

Users see the system too early
Testing becomes unnecessary

questions.question: Which input control would BEST detect a transposition error in an account number?

questions.question: A batch of 500 invoices is processed. Which control BEST confirms none were lost?

questions.question: A transaction fails halfway, leaving one account debited but the other not credited. Which database property was not met?

questions.question: Who should formally accept a new system before it goes live?

questions.question: Production customer data is copied to the test environment. What should the IS auditor expect?

Not the best answer. Reciprocal agreements are unreliable and slow.

questions.question: Which backup approach requires only the last full backup and the latest backup to restore?
choices: Full plus differential backups
Snapshots without full backups
Full plus incremental backups
Incremental backups only
questions.explanation: A differential contains all changes since the last full backup.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. A differential contains all changes since the last full backup.
Not the best answer. Snapshots alone may not be independent copies.
Not the best answer. Incremental restore needs every incremental since the full.
Not the best answer. Incrementals alone have no base.

questions.question: Backups complete successfully every night, but restores have never been tested. What is the MAIN risk?
choices: Data may not be recoverable when needed
Backup windows may be too long
Operators may forget the backup schedule
Backup storage costs may rise
questions.explanation: Without restore tests, there is no assurance backups are usable.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Without restore tests, there is no assurance backups are usable.
Not the best answer. Window length is secondary.
Not the best answer. Automation addresses schedules; recovery is the risk.
Not the best answer. Cost is secondary.

questions.question: Which control BEST protects backups from ransomware?
choices: Immutable or offline backup copies
Longer file names for backup sets
Storing backups on the same file server
Daily email confirmation of backups
questions.explanation: Immutable or offline copies cannot be encrypted by malware on the network.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Immutable or offline copies cannot be encrypted by malware on the network.
Not the best answer. File names are irrelevant.
Not the best answer. Same-server backups can be encrypted too.
Not the best answer. Emails do not protect data.

questions.question: Which is the FIRST step in developing a business continuity plan?
choices: Purchase backup generators
Select a recovery site
Perform a business impact analysis
Write team contact lists
questions.explanation: The BIA determines what must be recovered and how fast.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Equipment choices follow strategy.
Not the best answer. Site selection depends on BIA results.
Best answer. The BIA determines what must be recovered and how fast.
Not the best answer. Contact lists are part of the plan, later.

questions.question: Which test of a continuity plan carries the GREATEST operational risk?
choices: Checklist review
Table-top walk-through
Full interruption test
Simulation exercise
questions.explanation: Shutting down production to test recovery risks real disruption.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Checklists are paper reviews.
Not the best answer. Walk-throughs are discussion-based.
Best answer. Shutting down production to test recovery risks real disruption.
Not the best answer. Simulations do not stop production.

questions.question: Which recovery option is the LEAST reliable?
choices: Cloud-based disaster recovery service
Hot site contract
Reciprocal agreement with another company
Mirrored site
questions.explanation: Reciprocal agreements are hard to enforce and depend on the partner’s spare capacity.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Cloud DR is contracted and tested.
Not the best answer. Hot sites are contracted and ready.
Best answer. Reciprocal agreements are hard to enforce and depend on the partner’s spare capacity.
Not the best answer. Mirrored sites run in parallel.

questions.question: After a DR test, several recovery steps failed. What should the IS auditor verify NEXT?
choices: That the plan has been updated and the failed steps retested
That the next full test date was set for the same time next year and added to the calendar
That the team was thanked for participating
That the test report has been filed
questions.explanation: Testing is only useful if gaps are corrected and retested.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Testing is only useful if gaps are corrected and retested.
Not the best answer. Waiting a year leaves gaps open.
Not the best answer. Recognition is not a control.
Not the best answer. Filing does not fix gaps.

questions.question: What is the MOST important factor for a successful information security program?
choices: Visible commitment and support from senior management
Annual penetration tests
A large security team
The latest security tools from a leading vendor, deployed across all servers and endpoints
questions.explanation: Without senior management support, security lacks authority and resources.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Without senior management support, security lacks authority and resources.
Not the best answer. Testing is one activity, not a success factor.
Not the best answer. Team size does not ensure support.
Not the best answer. Tools without governance are ineffective.

questions.question: Which document should define minimum security settings for all Windows servers?
choices: A security baseline standard
The information security policy
The incident response plan
The acceptable use policy
questions.explanation: Baselines define minimum configurations for system types.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Baselines define minimum configurations for system types.
Not the best answer. The policy states intent at a high level.
Not the best answer. The IR plan covers incidents.
Not the best answer. Acceptable use addresses user behaviour.

questions.question: Which framework provides certifiable requirements for an information security management system?
choices: NIST SP 800-53
ITIL 4
ISO/IEC 27001
ISO/IEC 27002
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 27001 specifies ISMS requirements that can be certified.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. 800-53 is a control catalogue.
Not the best answer. ITIL covers service management.
Best answer. ISO/IEC 27001 specifies ISMS requirements that can be certified.
Not the best answer. 27002 is guidance on controls.

questions.question: Which control BEST prevents tailgating into a data centre?
choices: CCTV cameras at the entrance
A mantrap with single-person entry
Security awareness posters
A visitor sign-in book
questions.explanation: A mantrap physically allows only one person through at a time.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. CCTV detects but does not prevent.
Best answer. A mantrap physically allows only one person through at a time.
Not the best answer. Posters only raise awareness.
Not the best answer. Sign-in books do not stop tailgating.

questions.question: Which fire suppression approach is BEST for a data centre where water damage must be minimised?
choices: Halon system
Wet-pipe sprinklers
Portable fire extinguishers placed at every exit, with staff trained to use them
Clean-agent gas system or pre-action dry-pipe sprinklers
questions.explanation: Clean agents and pre-action systems reduce accidental water damage.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Halon is banned for environmental reasons.
Not the best answer. Wet-pipe systems hold water in pipes and can leak.
Not the best answer. Portables alone are insufficient.
Best answer. Clean agents and pre-action systems reduce accidental water damage.

questions.question: A data centre experiences short, sudden voltage increases. What is this called and what is the control?
choices: Spike; surge protection
Blackout; UPS only
Sag; raised floor
Brownout; generator
questions.explanation: Spikes are momentary voltage increases controlled by surge protectors.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Spikes are momentary voltage increases controlled by surge protectors.
Not the best answer. A blackout is total loss of power.
Not the best answer. A sag is a short voltage drop and floors do not help.
Not the best answer. A brownout is reduced voltage.

questions.question: Which is an example of multi-factor authentication?
choices: A password plus a one-time code from a hardware token
A PIN plus a memorised passphrase
A password plus a security question
Two different passwords
questions.explanation: MFA combines different factor types: something you know and something you have.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. MFA combines different factor types: something you know and something you have.
Not the best answer. Both are knowledge factors.
Not the best answer. Both are knowledge factors.
Not the best answer. Both are knowledge factors.

questions.question: Who should approve access to a finance application?
choices: The data or system owner in finance
The network administrator
The help desk analyst
The new user
questions.explanation: Owners know who needs access and are accountable for it.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Owners know who needs access and are accountable for it.
Not the best answer. Network staff lack business context.
Not the best answer. Help desk executes, not approves.
Not the best answer. Users cannot approve their own access.

questions.question: A biometric system has a high false acceptance rate. What is the MAIN concern?
choices: Unauthorized people may be granted access
Authorized users will be rejected more often
Enrolment will take longer
The system will cost more to maintain
questions.explanation: FAR measures impostors accepted, which is a security risk.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. FAR measures impostors accepted, which is a security risk.
Not the best answer. That describes false rejection.
Not the best answer. Enrolment speed is unrelated.
Not the best answer. Cost is secondary.

questions.question: Quarterly access reviews are performed, but managers approve all lists without changes. What is the MAIN concern?
choices: Reviews may be performed without real scrutiny of excessive access
The reviews take too long
The access lists are too short
Managers are not using the latest version of the identity governance software to approve the lists
questions.explanation: Rubber-stamp approvals mean inappropriate access may remain.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Rubber-stamp approvals mean inappropriate access may remain.
Not the best answer. Duration is secondary.
Not the best answer. List length is not the issue.
Not the best answer. Software version is irrelevant.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY principle of a zero-trust architecture?
choices: Trust all devices inside the corporate network and verify only connections that come from the internet
Allow administrators unrestricted access
Use one firewall at the perimeter
Never trust by default; verify every request continuously
questions.explanation: Zero trust removes implicit trust based on network location.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Internal trust is what zero trust removes.
Not the best answer. Unrestricted admin access contradicts least privilege.
Not the best answer. A single perimeter is the old model.
Best answer. Zero trust removes implicit trust based on network location.

questions.question: Where should a public web server be placed?
choices: Directly on the internet with no firewall
In a screened subnet (DMZ) between external and internal firewalls
On the internal network next to the customer database so that web pages load more quickly
On the same subnet as the payroll system
questions.explanation: A DMZ isolates public services from internal systems.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. No firewall leaves it unprotected.
Best answer. A DMZ isolates public services from internal systems.
Not the best answer. Internal placement exposes the network.
Not the best answer. Payroll should be isolated from public services.

questions.question: Which firewall type inspects the content of application traffic such as HTTP commands?
choices: Application-level (proxy) firewall
Circuit-level gateway
Packet-filtering firewall
Network address translation device
questions.explanation: Application gateways examine application-layer data.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Application gateways examine application-layer data.
Not the best answer. Circuit gateways control sessions, not content.
Not the best answer. Packet filters check headers only.
Not the best answer. NAT changes addresses.

questions.question: An IS auditor finds firewall rules allowing "any to any" traffic for a legacy server. What should be recommended?
choices: Document the rule as accepted
Replace the rule with specific, justified rules following least privilege
Move the server to the DMZ
Increase logging on the legacy server and keep the existing rule until the server is retired
questions.explanation: Overly permissive rules should be restricted to required traffic.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Acceptance without justification leaves risk.
Best answer. Overly permissive rules should be restricted to required traffic.
Not the best answer. Moving the server does not fix the rule.
Not the best answer. Logging does not prevent misuse.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY benefit of network segmentation?
choices: Reducing the number of users
Removing the need for firewalls between internal networks because each segment is trusted
Limiting the spread of an attack between parts of the network
Increasing internet bandwidth
questions.explanation: Segmentation contains compromises within zones.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. User numbers are unaffected.
Not the best answer. Segmentation uses firewalls and ACLs.
Best answer. Segmentation contains compromises within zones.
Not the best answer. Bandwidth is not the purpose.

questions.question: Before deploying data loss prevention, what should be done FIRST?
choices: Encrypt all email
Purchase the most expensive DLP tool
Classify data so DLP policies know what to protect
Block all USB ports
questions.explanation: DLP depends on knowing which data is sensitive.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Encrypting all email does not identify sensitive data.
Not the best answer. Cost does not ensure effectiveness.
Best answer. DLP depends on knowing which data is sensitive.
Not the best answer. USB blocking is one control, not the first step.

questions.question: DLP alerts are generated daily but never reviewed. What is the MAIN risk?
choices: The DLP licence will expire
Data leakage may occur without any response
Users will complain about frequent DLP warning messages and productivity will decrease
Storage costs will increase
questions.explanation: Alerts without response provide no protection.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Licensing is unrelated.
Best answer. Alerts without response provide no protection.
Not the best answer. Complaints are minor.
Not the best answer. Cost is secondary.

questions.question: A sender wants to guarantee that a message came from them and was not altered. What should they use?
choices: Encryption with the recipient’s public key
A digital signature using the sender’s private key
A checksum sent in the same email
Encryption with a shared symmetric key
questions.explanation: Signing with the private key gives authenticity, integrity and non-repudiation.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. That provides confidentiality.
Best answer. Signing with the private key gives authenticity, integrity and non-repudiation.
Not the best answer. An attacker can recompute a checksum.
Not the best answer. Shared keys do not prove who sent it.

questions.question: Which provides confidentiality for a message sent to a business partner?
choices: Signing it with the sender’s private key
Encrypting it with the partner’s public key
Compressing it before sending
Hashing it with SHA-256
questions.explanation: Only the partner’s private key can decrypt it.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Signing gives integrity, not confidentiality.
Best answer. Only the partner’s private key can decrypt it.
Not the best answer. Compression is not security.
Not the best answer. Hashing is not reversible encryption.

questions.question: What is a digital envelope?
choices: Data encrypted with a symmetric key that is itself encrypted with the recipient’s public key
A certificate issued by a CA
A signed hash of the message attached to an email so that the recipient can verify the sender
A password-protected zip file
questions.explanation: It combines fast symmetric encryption with secure key exchange.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. It combines fast symmetric encryption with secure key exchange.
Not the best answer. That is a certificate.
Not the best answer. That is a digital signature.
Not the best answer. Zip passwords are weak and not an envelope.

questions.question: Which is the GREATEST risk to a public key infrastructure?
choices: Slow certificate issuance
Large certificate revocation lists
Expiry of one user certificate
Compromise of the certificate authority’s private key
questions.explanation: A compromised CA key undermines trust in all certificates it issued.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Speed is operational.
Not the best answer. CRL size is manageable.
Not the best answer. One expiry affects one user.
Best answer. A compromised CA key undermines trust in all certificates it issued.

questions.question: A certificate is suspected to be compromised. What should happen?
choices: Revoke it and publish the revocation through CRL or OCSP
Change the certificate’s display name and serial number so that attackers cannot recognise it
Email users to stop trusting it
Wait for it to expire
questions.explanation: Revocation tells relying parties the certificate is no longer valid.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Revocation tells relying parties the certificate is no longer valid.
Not the best answer. Renaming does not revoke trust.
Not the best answer. Email is not a reliable trust mechanism.
Not the best answer. Waiting leaves it trusted.

questions.question: Under the shared responsibility model for IaaS, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system?
choices: The internet service provider
The cloud provider
The customer
The hypervisor vendor
questions.explanation: In IaaS the customer manages the OS and above.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. ISPs provide connectivity only.
Not the best answer. The provider manages physical infrastructure and virtualisation.
Best answer. In IaaS the customer manages the OS and above.
Not the best answer. The hypervisor vendor does not manage guests.

questions.question: Which is the MOST common cause of cloud data breaches?
choices: Failure of the provider’s power supply
Outdated provider marketing material
Misconfiguration of cloud resources such as storage permissions
Physical theft of disks and servers from the cloud provider’s data centres by insiders
questions.explanation: Customer misconfiguration is the leading cause of cloud exposure.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Power failure affects availability, not breaches.
Not the best answer. Marketing is irrelevant.
Best answer. Customer misconfiguration is the leading cause of cloud exposure.
Not the best answer. Physical theft is rare.

questions.question: What is the MAIN security concern specific to virtualisation?
choices: Slower backup times
Higher electricity use
Licence costs for the guest operating systems running inside each hosted virtual machine
Compromise of the hypervisor affecting all hosted virtual machines
questions.explanation: The hypervisor controls all VMs; its compromise breaks isolation.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Backup speed is operational.
Not the best answer. Power is not a security concern.
Not the best answer. Licensing is financial.
Best answer. The hypervisor controls all VMs; its compromise breaks isolation.

questions.question: A company allows employees to read email on personal phones. Which control is MOST important?
choices: Mobile device management with encryption, passcode and remote wipe
Disabling phone cameras
Allowing only one brand of phone
A policy requiring that personal phones are newer than two years and run the latest operating system
questions.explanation: MDM enforces protection of corporate data on devices.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. MDM enforces protection of corporate data on devices.
Not the best answer. Cameras are not the primary risk.
Not the best answer. Brand restriction does not secure data.
Not the best answer. Device age does not ensure security.

questions.question: Which wireless configuration is MOST secure for corporate users?
choices: WPA3-Enterprise with individual authentication
WEP with a long key
WPA2-Personal with a shared password
Hidden SSID with no encryption
questions.explanation: Enterprise mode uses individual credentials and strong encryption.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Enterprise mode uses individual credentials and strong encryption.
Not the best answer. WEP is broken.
Not the best answer. Shared passwords cannot be revoked per user.
Not the best answer. Hiding SSID is not security.

questions.question: IoT sensors in a warehouse use factory default passwords. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Document the default passwords in a protected spreadsheet so the operations team can find them
Replace all devices with a new brand
Change default credentials and place devices on a segmented network
Turn off the devices permanently
questions.explanation: Defaults are widely known; changing them and segmenting reduces exposure.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Documenting defaults leaves them exploitable.
Not the best answer. Replacement is not the first step.
Best answer. Defaults are widely known; changing them and segmenting reduces exposure.
Not the best answer. Shutting down removes business value.

questions.question: What is the BEST measure of an awareness program’s effectiveness?
choices: Number of slides in the course
The cost of the training vendor
Reduction in risky behaviour, such as lower phishing simulation click rates
Training attendance on the first day of the program and the number of completion certificates issued
questions.explanation: Effectiveness is shown by changed behaviour.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Content volume is not effectiveness.
Not the best answer. Cost is not a measure of effect.
Best answer. Effectiveness is shown by changed behaviour.
Not the best answer. Attendance shows reach only.

questions.question: An employee receives a call from someone claiming to be IT support asking for their password. What type of attack is this?
choices: Social engineering (pretexting)
Salami attack
Brute force attack
Denial of service
questions.explanation: The attacker uses a false pretext to manipulate a person.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. The attacker uses a false pretext to manipulate a person.
Not the best answer. Salami skims small amounts.
Not the best answer. Brute force guesses passwords technically.
Not the best answer. DoS disrupts availability.

questions.question: Which control BEST protects against eavesdropping on network traffic?
choices: Installing antivirus software
Using longer passwords
Encrypting data in transit
Running vulnerability scans
questions.explanation: Encryption keeps captured traffic unreadable.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Antivirus targets malware.
Not the best answer. Passwords protect accounts, not traffic.
Best answer. Encryption keeps captured traffic unreadable.
Not the best answer. Scans find weaknesses but do not protect traffic.

questions.question: A program in a payroll system rounds down each salary by a fraction of a cent and diverts the remainder. What is this?
choices: Salami attack
Piggybacking
Logic bomb
Trojan horse
questions.explanation: Salami attacks take tiny amounts from many transactions.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. Salami attacks take tiny amounts from many transactions.
Not the best answer. Piggybacking is physical or session tailgating.
Not the best answer. A logic bomb triggers on a condition.
Not the best answer. A trojan hides malicious function in a legitimate program.

questions.question: What is the MOST important prerequisite before a penetration test?
choices: Informing all employees in advance
Disabling the intrusion detection system so that it does not interfere with the testing activities
Written authorisation from management defining scope and rules of engagement
Purchasing commercial testing tools
questions.explanation: Testing without authorisation may be illegal and disruptive.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Wide notice may invalidate realistic testing.
Not the best answer. Disabling IDS removes protection.
Best answer. Testing without authorisation may be illegal and disruptive.
Not the best answer. Tools are secondary.

questions.question: Which is the PRIMARY benefit of a SIEM?
choices: Correlating events from many sources to detect security incidents
Managing software licences
Encrypting stored data
Replacing the need for firewalls and intrusion prevention systems at the network perimeter
questions.explanation: SIEM aggregates and correlates logs to generate meaningful alerts.
choiceExplanations: Best answer. SIEM aggregates and correlates logs to generate meaningful alerts.
Not the best answer. Licence management is unrelated.
Not the best answer. Encryption is a different control.
Not the best answer. It complements firewalls.

questions.question: An anomaly-based intrusion detection system has been installed. What is its MAIN drawback?
choices: It blocks traffic automatically
Inability to detect new attacks
Higher rate of false positives until it is tuned
No need for a baseline
questions.explanation: Anomaly detection flags deviations, which can include legitimate activity.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. IDS alerts; IPS blocks.
Not the best answer. Anomaly IDS can detect new attacks.
Best answer. Anomaly detection flags deviations, which can include legitimate activity.
Not the best answer. It needs a baseline.

questions.question: A ransomware infection is detected on two workstations. What should the incident response team do FIRST?
choices: Restore all servers from backup
Pay the ransom to recover the encrypted files quickly and avoid any interruption to the business
Notify all customers immediately
Contain the infection by isolating the affected workstations
questions.explanation: Containment limits spread before eradication and recovery.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Restoring before containment risks reinfection.
Not the best answer. Paying is not a response step and is discouraged.
Not the best answer. Notification depends on assessment.
Best answer. Containment limits spread before eradication and recovery.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of the lessons-learned phase of incident response?
choices: Closing the incident ticket
Calculating insurance claims
Improving controls and procedures to prevent recurrence
Identifying the members of staff responsible so that disciplinary action can be taken
questions.explanation: Lessons learned feed improvements to the security program.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Closing tickets is administrative.
Not the best answer. Insurance is secondary.
Best answer. Lessons learned feed improvements to the security program.
Not the best answer. Blame is not the purpose.

questions.question: A forensic investigator needs to analyse a suspect’s hard drive. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Copy important documents to a USB drive
Run antivirus on the original disk
Create a bit-for-bit image and verify it with a hash
Boot the computer and browse the most recent files to decide whether a full investigation is needed
questions.explanation: Working on a verified image preserves original evidence.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Selective copying loses evidence and integrity.
Not the best answer. Scanning the original may alter it.
Best answer. Working on a verified image preserves original evidence.
Not the best answer. Booting changes data on the disk.

questions.question: Why is chain of custody important in digital forensics?
choices: It replaces the need for hashing because every handover of the evidence is already documented
It reduces storage costs
It shows the evidence was controlled and unaltered from collection to court
It speeds up analysis
questions.explanation: Chain of custody supports the admissibility and integrity of evidence.
choiceExplanations: Not the best answer. Hashing and custody work together.
Not the best answer. Storage cost is unrelated.
Best answer. Chain of custody supports the admissibility and integrity of evidence.
Not the best answer. It does not speed analysis.
